title: Residential Painting in Trenton, FL | Precision Paint
description: Residential painting in Trenton FL that starts with a moisture and repair check. Own crews, two-coat premium systems, and a signed punch walk at the end.
heroIntro: We repaint Trenton homes inside and out, and we start by finding the soft wood and wet spots that would ruin new paint within a few summers.

sections.h2: A house repaint is a repair job first
body: Good residential painting in Trenton FL begins with a probe and a meter long before any sprayer comes off the truck. Walking your Gilchrist County lot, the crew lead jabs at fascia and soffit boards hunting for punky wood, studies the spots where rain pools at sills and door thresholds, and reads each stucco crack to decide if it is cosmetic or a true repair. Those findings go on the estimate as separate lines, so you see what the repair pass costs apart from the paint.
Skip that step and a fresh coat ends up peeling over rotten wood two years later. Swapping a bad length of fascia today is cheaper for you than chasing blisters on it later.

sections.h2: Homes in town and homes out on the land
body: Around downtown Trenton, houses tend to sit close to the street and to each other, which makes overspray control and careful masking part of the plan. Closer to the Suwannee and out toward Hart Springs, heavy tree cover holds moisture against the walls, so those houses get a mildew kill before any primer goes on. On rural homesteads the scope often stretches to porches and railings, and we can add deck staining at the same visit.

sections.h2: The product system on a Trenton home
body: On a Trenton house, each material gets its own coating. Lap siding and trim take a top-grade 100% acrylic; stucco with hairline movement takes an elastomeric; front doors and porch railings take a waterborne urethane enamel that cures tough. Bare porch posts or rails left natural get a penetrating stain instead of paint. Plan on two full coats, and wherever we spray rough or porous surfaces, a painter follows behind with a brush or roller to push the coating into the grain. Inside the house, low-VOC paint is an option.
bullets: Scrape and sand loose paint, then prime any bare wood
New fascia where boards are rotten, re-set nail pops, fresh caulk at gaps
A pair of finish coats from Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore, with the exact line written into your quote
Site tidied each evening, plus a closing walk-around you sign off on

sections.h2: How long it takes, and living through it
body: For the outside of a Trenton home, figure three to seven working days once washing and dry time are done. Doing every room inside takes anywhere from three days to two weeks. Your family stays put the whole time: painters slide and drape the furniture and keep work confined to one room at once. Prefer to tackle the inside first? Read about interior painting in Trenton. For the broader service, visit residential painting, or return to the Trenton overview. Wondering whether your boards are wet underneath? Our write-up on moisture trapped behind siding lists the signs.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted trim, or just paint it?
faqs.a: Rotten boards come out and new ones go in; paint never covers decay on our jobs. You will see each replacement priced as a separate item on the quote you approve.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with a Trenton house repaint?
faqs.a: Trenton exteriors are covered by our written workmanship guarantee for as long as 10 years, sitting on top of what the paint maker provides. Labelled cans of your colors stay behind for future touch-ups.

faqs.q: When is the best time to paint the outside of my house in Trenton?
faqs.a: Fall through spring, roughly October to May, gives the most forgiving drying weather here. A July or August job can still happen; crews simply start at sunrise and keep watch on the dew point and radar.
